decision: treat the pasted Shed findings and assessment as one release program
why: the requested end state spans contract safety, lifecycle, wallet behavior, submission policy, and proof
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
result: five independently verifiable stages

decision: start with replay and price isolation
why: two executable counterexamples disprove the core value-safety guarantee
evidence: docs/review/run-counterexamples.sh
result: contract stage in progress

decision: use durable state keyed by offerId
why: it preserves the current shared-appData bundle and directly models single-use plus future cancellation
evidence: 54 local tests and 5 mainnet-fork tests pass
result: changed-appData replay and independent-price settlement now revert

decision: give every relay its own scratch directory
why: `relay` never wrote its input, so creating offer B made offer A's acceptance relay B's computation
evidence: docs/review/service-counterexamples.mjs relaying A with B on disk
result: per-attempt LINK_COMPUTED_FILE/LINK_SIGNATURES_FILE; paths overridable in every script

decision: require order, receipt and consumed state for "settled"
why: a balance decrease reported settlement for an unrelated withdrawal
evidence: docs/review/service-counterexamples.mjs
result: status has no balance read; settled needs all three pieces of evidence

decision: cancel through the owning Shed, not a wrapper-only flag
why: revoking the ComposableCoW authorization and the offer must be one transaction or neither
result: test_makerCancellationAtomicallyRevokesOrderAndOffer: order removed, offer Cancelled, settle reverts

decision: build the lifecycle harness before claiming the stage green
why: contract-level tests cannot see interleaving, restart or retry behaviour
evidence: docs/review/service-lifecycle.mjs
result: 9 checks over real HTTP against fake forge/cast and a fixture orderbook

decision: every cast/forge file input gets a private temp file
why: all typed-data checks shared out-json/verify.json; two service instances over one store verified each other's messages
evidence: restoring the shared path fails the two-instance lifecycle check
result: `withScratch`; no fixed scratch path left in the service

decision: refuse a second in-flight acceptance in the same process
why: the await on the order round trip let a second request relay and post again
evidence: concurrent-acceptance lifecycle check failed 202/202, now 202/409 with one order post
result: `accepting` set; a store-level lock is still open for multi-instance deployment

decision: escape untrusted text before it reaches the DOM
why: a token's symbol is chosen by whoever deployed the token and lands on a signing page
evidence: pre-fix, a symbol containing an runs script: docs/review/page-safety.mjs
result: `esc` in both pages; real-Chrome check asserts no element and no execution

decision: describe the allowance as exact or unlimited
why: a DAI-style permit carries `allowed: true` and no amount, so "approve exactly this amount" is false
evidence: funding() reports allowance: exact|unlimited; the page says "any amount of this token, until you revoke it"
result: one decision in funding(); the role view reports its conclusion instead of re-deriving it

decision: fund by approve when no permit signature can exist
why: personal_sign over a raw EIP-712 digest adds the EIP-191 header, so the signature recovers to another address and no contract accepts it
evidence: pre-fix the page offered that path; now mode=approve with the calldata to send
result: server builds approve(spender, amount); the page sends it and polls the allowance, not the tx hash

decision: gate signing on the wallet's chain
why: the trade is signed for one chain and a wallet on another produces a signature that chain rejects
evidence: page-safety check: `?chain` mismatch disables the signing button and names both chains
result: walletChain read at connect and on chainChanged

decision: drive the real page in headless Chrome with no dependency
why: escaping, chain gating and the approve flow are invisible to a syntax check and to a function-level test
evidence: Node's global WebSocket speaks CDP; 5 checks pass and each fails when its fix is reverted
result: docs/review/page-safety.mjs

decision: decode `cast` string output as JSON instead of trimming quotes
why: a symbol containing a quote or backslash kept the escapes, so the page displayed them
evidence: `castString` in the server, exercised by the malicious-symbol check
result: one place that reads a string return value

decision: run the real e2e before adding a testnet
why: the local offline stack is a real chain plus the real CoW services, and a public testnet needs CoW's allowlist key
evidence: script/DeployPrivateTrade.s.sol: allowlisting is a manager action; scripts impersonate it
result: environment/colima.md

decision: read the e2e's typed data from the service, not a scratch file
why: the service stopped writing out-json/link-computed.json, so the check compared today's digest to a stale payload from another offer
evidence: the real run failed with "the typed data for the maker's bundle is not the same message as its digest"; it passes now
result: view_field() reads /offers/:id/role

decision: add a cancellation leg to the link e2e
why: cancellation was the one contract fix with no real-chain proof
evidence: second offer cancelled on-chain, wrapper reports cancelled, retry converges
result: scripts/link-service-e2e.sh section 6

decision: run the flow with a real wallet extension, and verify the settlement independently
why: the last unproven step, and where wallet quirks actually show
evidence: real wallet run settled tx 0x31d6c066…: receipt status 1 sent by the relayer, wrapper consumed, order fulfilled, neither party's nonce moved
result: docs/WALLET.md

decision: label the counterparty as their order contract, not as the person
why: the page showed the other party's Shed under the heading "Counterparty", which reads like the person you are dealing with
evidence: page-safety check asserts the Shed address is shown, named as a CoW Shed, and explicitly not their wallet
result: the other side / their order owner

decision: the wallet run rendered readable EIP-712, so nothing is left unproven in stages 1-3
why: the prompts are the one thing a fixture cannot check
evidence: COWShed domain, ExecuteHooks message, no gas prompt, no transaction
result: docs/WALLET.md

decision: assert exact four-way deltas and zero Shed residue, not just "it moved"
why: received balance increased passes on a wrong amount, a wrong direction, or money stuck in a contract
evidence: each wallet moved by exactly the agreed amount; all four Shed balances unchanged
result: scripts/link-service-e2e.sh

decision: run the regression gates in CI, not just forge test
why: the contract, service and browser regressions are exactly what forge test cannot see
evidence: bash docs/review/run-counterexamples.sh runs on every push; the fork suite on manual dispatch
result: .github/workflows/test.yml

decision: one private trade window at a time
why: the published context is the guarantee, and wrappedSettle is vendored upstream with no reentrancy guard
evidence: ReentrantSolverToken re-enters during transferFrom; without the guard the revert is PrivateTrade_OfferConsumed, with it PrivateTrade_Reentered
result: test_reentrantTokenCannotOpenASecondWindow fails when the guard is removed

decision: emit the authorisation with the terms decoded
why: a party signs the terms as createChecked calldata, which a wallet shows as hex, so nothing on-chain said what it authorised
evidence: vm.expectEmit with the Shed as the emitter: shed, owner, role, offerId and the full terms
result: PrivateTradeOrderAuthorised and authoriser.describe give a reader the same answer

decision: check bundle signatures by owner kind, not by ecrecover
why: a Safe-owned Shed's valid signature recovers to an unrelated address, so a service pre-check reads it as a wrong signature
evidence: ShedBundle.validSignature branches on owner code the way LibAuthenticatedHooks does; recover() is asserted to differ for a Safe
result: removing the branch makes test_bundleSignatureCheckHandlesBothOwnerKinds fail

decision: a Safe owns a Shed, and needs a fallback handler to authenticate it
why: the Shed's admin is any address, and a Safe answers ERC-1271 through its fallback handler; without one the query returns nothing
evidence: SafeProxy + ExtensibleFallbackHandler, owner signs the Safe message of the ExecuteHooks digest: settlement, cancellation, beneficiary and refusal cases all tested for EOA and Safe owners
result: test_safeOwnedShedSettlesAndPaysTheSafe; signing the raw digest instead reverts GS026

decision: refuse offchainInput and answer PollNever for a dead offer
why: ComposableCoW requires a handler to validate offchainInput and watch towers classify orders from PollNever/OrderNotValid
evidence: verify and getTradeableOrder revert PrivateTrade_UnexpectedOffchainInput; a cancelled or expired offer reports PollNever
result: privateTradeHandler suite, 6 tests

decision: the offer salt is fresh random bytes from the maker's browser
why: ComposableCoW requires a cryptographically secure salt, and it is the offer identity, the derived ComposableCoW salt and the hook nonce
evidence: page.mjs draws it with crypto.getRandomValues; server.mjs validates it or draws its own; LinkCompute refuses a request without one
result: PrivateTradeBuilder tests: a different salt is a different offer, a reused salt is the same offer

decision: check what can be checked before a signature is taken
why: a wallet prompt is expensive to take back, and the offerbook path discovers every problem after both prompts
evidence: role view reports ready{}; /signature and /accept refuse 409 while it fails; 5 checks, each one the settlement's own test
result: docs/review/service-lifecycle.mjs: an offer that cannot settle is refused before a signature is taken

decision: simulate the relay before broadcasting it
why: forge stops at the first call that would fail, so a bad signature or a spent nonce costs nothing to find out
evidence: relay() runs without --broadcast first; RELAY_DRY_RUN=0 skips it
result: fixture fails only the dry run: 502, no broadcast, no order posted

decision: a contract owner funds by approval, never by a permit
why: a token permit is verified by ecrecover inside the token, so a smart account cannot produce one
evidence: funding() reads cast code on the owner; approve mode, with the reason named, before the prompt
result: page-safety: contract account shows the smart-account note and never the permit step

decision: ask a contract owner for its signature instead of recovering it
why: ShedBundle.validSignature branches exactly as LibAuthenticatedHooks does
evidence: LinkRelay now uses validSignature; the service calls isValidSignature and accepts blobs longer than 65 bytes
result: lifecycle: the blob the account accepts is taken, any other is refused

decision: take the in-flight acceptance lock after every early return
why: the lock was taken before checks that return, so a refused acceptance wedged the offer as "already in flight" forever
evidence: lifecycle: 403, then a short signature 400, then a valid 202
result: accepting.add moved to immediately before the work

decision: collecting a Safe's owners is the Safe's job, not ours
why: a 2-of-3 Safe gathers its owners through its own tooling and returns one blob; blocking it was wrong
evidence: threshold and owner count are reported, never gating; a longer blob is accepted and judged by asking the account
result: lifecycle: contract account decides its own threshold, and its blob is taken as it comes

decision: ask a contract account for a Safe message, not the trade's typed data
why: the handler checks its owners over hashMessage(digest), so the trade's own typed data produces a signature it refuses
evidence: page signs SafeMessage(bytes message) with the digest; browser check reads the request it made
result: page-safety: a smart contract account is asked for a Safe message

decision: syntax-check the fixture programs too
why: four times an unescaped backtick in a comment broke a program built inside a template literal
evidence: scripts/check-page.mjs now checks the fake forge and cast as well
result: it caught a fifth one on the next run

decision: deploy through the canonical CREATE2 proxy under one fixed salt
why: a dry run must print the address a broadcast produces, and one audit and one allowlist entry must cover Sepolia and mainnet
evidence: the first version predicted from the deployer EOA and the real dry run deployed elsewhere: forge's new{salt} goes through 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C, the deployer key is not an input
result: test_derivationMatchesFoundrysOwn; dry run on live mainnet state prints the pinned four

decision: freeze the four addresses in a test
why: the audit report and the allowlist entry describe one bytecode at one address, so drift has to fail loudly
evidence: the script requires the deployed address to equal the predicted one and the test pins all four
result: any change to a contract, constructor or salt fails PrivateTradeDeployTest until re-pinned

decision: write manifests only in a broadcast
why: a dry run must not overwrite the addresses the offline stack and the service read
evidence: vm.isContext(ScriptBroadcast) || ScriptResume; out-json/private-trade-deployed.json untouched by a dry run
result: a dry run against mainnet wrote nothing

decision: sign the authorisation, not the allowance
why: a per-trade approve puts a token allowance inside the calldata the party signs; a standing allowance is a separate, revocable decision
evidence: ShedBundle.authorisationOnly / approvalOnly; test_standingAllowanceNeedsNoApproveInTheBundle settles with a one-call bundle after a standing approval
result: the trade signature is one call; the allowance is its own transaction

decision: put the settlement window in transient storage
why: with persistent storage a future early return between opening and closing the window would leave it open forever, and every later settlement would revert
evidence: measured: 1,120,033 transient vs 1,116,452 persistent in test_settlesWithShedOwnedOrders
result: impossible cross-transaction leak for +0.3% gas

decision: prove the fill, not just that the settlement returned
why: validating calldata proves the orders were right; it does not prove GPv2 recorded a fill, and a bundle that returns without delivering is the framework's own warning
evidence: filledAmount read for both legs before and after; deriving the UID from the wrong owner reverts every settlement test with PrivateTrade_SettlementDidNotFill
result: _open/_close, FillGuard

decision: re-pin all four CREATE2 addresses
why: the wrapper's bytecode moved, and the handler's init code embeds the wrapper address, so the submitter and authoriser moved too
result: test_addressesArePinned now passes
